item.title: Bank rate increased to 4% - November 2026 Monetary Policy Summary and Minutes

rating.summary: The Bank of England's MPC voted 8-1 to raise Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 4% at its November 2026 meeting, driven by surging energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict pushing UK CPI inflation to 3.5% and forecast to reach ~5% by mid-2027. The sole dissenter, Catherine Mann, preferred a larger 50bp hike on risk-management and credibility grounds. The Committee signalled it is not on a pre-set path but that further tightening may be warranted depending on the evolution of second-round effects, energy prices, and domestic wage and price dynamics.
rating.stance_rationale: The decision represents a clear hawkish action—a rate hike with a majority signalling openness to further tightening—but the Committee's emphasis on data-dependence, absence of second-round effects so far, and one member explicitly framing the move as a 'one-for-now' insurance hike tempers the hawkishness somewhat, placing it at a moderately hawkish rather than strongly hawkish reading.
key_quotes: The duration and scale of the energy price increase had generated sufficient inflationary pressures in the pipeline to warrant an increase in Bank Rate.
Achieving the level of Bank Rate necessary to confront challenges and risks to lasting achievement of the 2% inflation target is likely to require more policy tightening, including in the near term.
